newsitem.title: CHINA: China says 70 pct of certificate bonds sold.
newsitem.headline: China says 70 pct of certificate bonds sold.

text.p: China had sold more than 85.7 billion yuan ($10.3 billion) worth of certificate bonds by June 3 but must boost marketing if it is to sell the full quota for the year, the Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.
The figure accounted for 69.68 percent of the amount that the government has said it would issue this year, Xinhua said.
Certificate bonds were likely to be sold out before the issue closes in October, Xinhua quoted Shang Fulin, deputy governor of the People's Bank of China, or central bank, as saying.
However, sales of two-, three- and five-year certificate bonds have slowed since March, he said.
He attributed the slowdown to investors diverting capital to the surging stock market since the start of the year and to competition from corporate bonds, which carry a higher interest rate.
The stock indices of Shenzhen and Shanghai soared more than 45 percent each before May when the government banned state enterprises and listed companies from speculating in stocks, Xinhua said.
China has set a quota of 15 billion yuan for corporate bonds issues in 1997, it said.
The government plans to issue another 60 billion yuan worth of government bonds in the second half of the year, it said.
Two-year treasury bonds have proved more popular than five-year bonds, Xinhua said.
Official figures show 86 percent of the 25 billion yuan in two-year bonds has been snapped up compared with only 53 percent for 25 billion yuan in five-year bonds.
